gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-marchen: Heavy, blunt letters from Plakkaat hit first, their curled terminals nearly closing on the stem. Noto Sans Marchen takes over with small letters standing almost capital-tall, its curves ending in clear daylight.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-mayan-n: Plakkaat draws every line like a bent straw, with terminals curling round until they nearly touch the stem. Against that tight finish, Noto Sans Mayan Numerals gapes wide.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-medefai: Bold and heavy, Plakkaat curls its terminals inward while Noto Sans Medefaidrin lifts its lowercase high with open curves. Make the heading small and that closed density crowds.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-meetei-: Plakkaat looks thin-lined yet heavy, every stroke like a bent straw with no thinner parts. Noto Sans Meetei Mayek cracks its rounds open like a bangle and gives its large lowercase eyes room to breathe.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-mende-k: Modern and clean, Noto Sans Mende Kikakui lets daylight through every curve while its lowercase stands tall against the capitals. Plakkaat does the heavy, closed-up shouting; this one does the open talking.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-meroiti: Chunky and curled up tight, Plakkaat is the loud one here. Noto Sans Meroitic is the approachable sans-serif, with see-through c openings and lowercase that fills the line like capitals.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-modi: Plakkaat's lines bend like straws, with terminals sweeping round to almost touch the stem, and it carries real weight. Noto Sans Modi lets daylight into every curve, so the plain sans feels open beside it.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-mono: Noto Sans Mono spaces its sturdy, tall lowercase generously, with every curve left wide open and no letters bumping. Plakkaat does heavy and closed; this sans-serif does open and spacious.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-mro: Heavy Plakkaat bends its lines like straws, terminals curling nearly shut. Then Noto Sans Mro brings dense, tall-middled words with large entrances into each letter, the plain sans doing the opening up.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-gf-noto-sans-multani: Thick, curled and heavy, Plakkaat keeps stems and arches identical in thickness with closed-up terminals. Noto Sans Multani is the open one, a lofty x-height and an e with a wide gap.
